links.note: 8, 15, 17 satisfies 64 + 225 = 289; the question names the Pythagorean triple outright.

625 among 1057, 7928 and 64000 - none small enough to be recognised from the familiar list, so the m = n-squared definition has to be applied to a four- or five-digit number. That is 31335, not the 1,4,9,16,25 recall of 31334.
Asks which of 19, 11, 24, 13 squares to a number with 6 at the units place; 24 squared is 576. It is answered from the units digit alone, the quick test this concept supplies.
1+3+5+7 = 16: the sum of successive odd numbers from 1 landing on a square, which is the fact this concept states.
9 squared minus 1 = 80 needs only 9 times 9, a number multiplied by itself.
42 squared = 1764. This concept names 42 explicitly as one the (40+2) tens-and-units split handles without multiplying 42 by 42.
Picks 24 out of 4, 9 and 16 - all three distractors are in the 1, 4, 9, 16, 25 list this concept gives, so recognition from that list settles it.
23 squared = 529 is this concept's own worked example: (20+3) squared expanding to 400+60+60+9.
Only 2826 is even, so only its square is even. The decision is made from the last digit of each candidate, which is what this concept studies.
81 against 45, 18 and 54: 81 is 9 times 9, recognised from the small square numbers.
The one's digit of 1234 squared is 6 because 4 squared ends in 6 - the units digit alone decides it.
Finding 36 as the only square between 30 and 40 is the same reasoning this concept uses on 32: 5 squared is 25, 6 squared is 36, so nothing else in the gap can be a square.
Which of 19, 24, 25, 13 squares to a 6 at the units place - 24 squared is 576, decided on the last digit.
18 numbers lie between 9 squared and 10 squared, i.e. 2n with n = 9 - this concept's count, applied rather than counted out.
(-9) times (-9) = 81: a number multiplied by itself, with the sign of the product the only wrinkle.
Square root of 6400 is 80 - asking which number squared gives 6400, i.e. undoing the squaring. No factorisation or long division is needed at this size.
48 = 2^4 x 3 has one unpaired 3, so dividing by 3 leaves 16 with every prime paired. The answer comes straight from the pairing of prime factors.
The smallest three-digit square is 100 = 10 squared, read off the table of squares of 1 to 20 where the three-digit entries begin.
99 squared is 9801 and 100 squared is 10000, so 9801 is the largest four-digit square. Same exclusion-between-consecutive-squares argument as the 32 example.
AB=6, BC=8 gives AC=10; 6, 8, 10 is a Pythagorean triplet and the squares answer a question about a triangle.
LCM of 4, 9 and 10 is 180 = 2^2 x 3^2 x 5, whose 5 is unpaired; supplying the missing 5 gives 900. The work is entirely in pairing prime factors.
18 is the non-square among 81, 100 and 121, all recognisable as a number times itself.
A 3 by 4 rectangle has a 5 cm diagonal - the 3, 4, 5 triplet this concept introduces, used on a real figure.
Square root of 169 is 13: undoing the squaring. The distractors 1.3 and 1310 test only that the inverse operation is understood, not any method.
A number ending in 9 has a square ending in 1, since 9 squared is 81 - a property of the ending digit.
(-95) squared = 9025 is a(a+1) hundreds plus 25 with a = 9: 90 hundreds plus 25. This concept's rule for numbers ending in 5, and it is why 7225 (85 squared) is offered as the trap.
